Touring on a Budget

You do not need to spend fifteen thousand pounds on a new BMW to enjoy fantastic motorcycle touring in the UK. The used market is packed with capable, reliable touring bikes at a fraction of the new price. With five thousand pounds or less, you can find machines that will comfortably carry you and your luggage from Land's End to John o'Groats and back.

What to Look For in a Budget Tourer

  • Service history — A well-maintained bike with documented service records is worth more than a lower-mileage machine with no history.
  • Shaft drive vs chain — Shaft drive bikes save chain maintenance costs and hassle on tour. Honda, BMW, and Yamaha all offer shaft-drive tourers in this price range.
  • Parts availability — Stick to popular models with readily available parts. Obscure bikes can become expensive nightmares when something breaks mid-tour.
  • Tyre and consumable costs — Check the price of tyres and brake pads for your chosen bike. Some models have significantly cheaper running costs than others.

Best Used Tourers Under Five Thousand Pounds

Honda CB500X (2019-2022) — The A2-friendly adventure tourer that punches well above its weight. Reliable, fuel-efficient, light, and surprisingly comfortable for long distances. Under three thousand pounds buys a low-mileage example with ABS.

Suzuki V-Strom 650 (2017-2021) — The unsung hero of budget touring. Comfortable, reliable, fuel-efficient, and blessed with a smooth V-twin engine. The aftermarket support is enormous and luggage systems are readily available secondhand.

Kawasaki Versys 650 (2015-2020) — A versatile parallel twin that handles everything from commuting to touring. Comfortable ergonomics, decent wind protection with the optional taller screen, and lively engine character make it engaging on B-roads.

BMW F 700 GS (2013-2018) — BMW touring credentials at a budget price. The parallel twin is unstressed and reliable, shaft drive eliminates chain hassle, and the adventure styling gives good weather protection. Under four thousand pounds for good examples.

Yamaha Tracer 700 (2016-2020) — The CP2 parallel twin engine is a gem — torquey, economical, and characterful. The Tracer platform adds touring comfort and wind protection. Arguably the best value touring bike in this price bracket.

With five thousand pounds, budget approximately three to four thousand for the bike and keep one to two thousand in reserve for essential upgrades like luggage, tyres, and a full service before your first tour.

Essential Upgrades for Budget Tourers

A taller screen improves wind protection dramatically. Aftermarket heated grips are cheap and transform cold-weather comfort. Budget soft panniers from Kriega or Oxford provide luggage capacity without the cost of hard cases. New tyres before a tour are essential for safety and confidence.
keyTakeaways: Five thousand pounds buys a capable used tourer with money left for luggage and tyres.
The Honda CB500X is A2-friendly and available under three thousand pounds with ABS.
Shaft-drive options like the BMW F 700 GS cut chain maintenance on a budget.
The Yamaha Tracer 700 CP2 twin is arguably the best value in the bracket.
Budget three to four thousand for the bike and hold reserve for a service and upgrades.

faq.q: Can I tour on an A2-licence budget bike?
faq.a: Yes. The Honda CB500X is A2-compliant with restriction, light, economical and comfortable enough for long distances. It handles motorway runs and week-long tours well, and low-mileage examples with ABS sell for under three thousand pounds.

faq.q: How much should I keep back for upgrades?
faq.a: Budget roughly three to four thousand for the bike itself and keep one to two thousand in reserve. That covers a pre-tour service, fresh tyres, soft panniers from Kriega or Oxford, heated grips and a taller screen, which together transform a budget bike into a genuine tourer.

faq.q: Is service history more important than mileage?
faq.a: Yes. A well-maintained bike with documented service records is worth more than a lower-mileage machine with no history. Check the stamped book, MOT history online and evidence of major items like valve adjustments before buying.

faq.q: Which budget tourer is cheapest to run?
faq.a: The Yamaha Tracer 700 and Honda CB500X are both very frugal thanks to their efficient parallel twins. Shaft-drive options like the BMW F 700 GS save on chain replacement, though tyre and pad prices vary, so check consumable costs for your chosen model before committing.
